executiveSummary: Available reporting indicates persistent, geographically distributed GNSS interference and spoofing affecting bridge navigation and AIS integrity in the Persian Gulf/Strait of Hormuz, Baltic Sea near Gdansk, and off the U.S. West Coast. This creates a credible safety-of-navigation risk and warrants immediate bridge procedure reinforcement. Confidence: High. U.S. maritime authorities warn that foreign-manufactured port equipment and logistics platforms can introduce exploitable pathways into port IT/OT, elevating supply chain and terminal operations risk. Confidence: High. Facts from sources: MARAD reports significant, continuing GNSS interference/spoofing in the Persian Gulf/Strait of Hormuz/Gulf of Oman with safety implications Maritime Advisory . NAVCEN user reports corroborate regional GPS disruption across Arabian Sea and Persian Gulf traffic Supporting Report . NAVCEN reporting indicates GPS jamming/spoofing near Gdansk Harbor and in the Baltic Sea with position displacement; multiple systems may be affected Supporting Report . gCaptain documents GNSS interference off California with anomalous AIS tracks for commercial vessels View Article . MARAD warns that foreign-linked cranes, inspection systems, and logistics platforms (e.g., LOGINK, Nuctech, ZPMC ecosystems) may expose sensitive data and IT/OT pathways in ports Maritime Advisory . U.S. Coast Guard guidance clarifies that low physical-security risk does not equate to low cyber risk under 33 CFR Part 101 Subpart F for MTSA-regulated entities Government Advisory . Progress confirmed a zero-day in ShareFile Storage Zones Controller with emergency operational guidance and subsequent patches; maritime logistics users may be affected Vendor/Industry Report . Federal agencies broadened an alert on Iran-linked OT targeting across industrial environments, relevant to maritime OT operators View Article . Analytical assessment: The collected intelligence supports an assessment that navigation integrity risks are elevated across three regions, increasing the likelihood of loss-of-view or incorrect ECDIS inputs if bridges rely solely on GNSS/AIS. Confidence: High. Port and terminal operators should assume increased exploitation interest in connected crane and logistics ecosystems and verify compliance with Coast Guard directives. Confidence: High. Enterprise file-transfer vulnerabilities (ShareFile) continue to create supply-chain exposure pathways into maritime business operations. Confidence: Medium. Outlook: Continued reporting on GNSS anomalies in the Middle East and Baltic regions is likely over the next 72 hours; operators transiting affected areas should maintain manual cross-checks and report anomalies Maritime Advisory NAVCEN . U.S. regulatory posture on maritime cybersecurity (33 CFR Subpart F) suggests heightened scrutiny of cyber risk assumptions for MTSA-regulated vessels and facilities Government Advisory . Confidence: High.
keyFindings: GNSS interference/spoofing is active in the Persian Gulf/Strait of Hormuz/Gulf of Oman, with safety-of-navigation implications. Maritime Advisory
Baltic Sea traffic near Gdansk continues to encounter GPS jamming/spoofing with position displacement and multi-system effects in related reports. NAVCEN GUIDE
GNSS interference off California produced anomalous AIS tracks for commercial vessels, underscoring global exposure. gCaptain
Foreign-manufactured port technologies and logistics platforms present material cyber and supply-chain risks to maritime IT/OT. MARAD Advisory
U.S. Coast Guard clarifies that low physical-security waivers do not imply low cyber risk under 33 CFR Part 101 Subpart F; reassessment is required. USCG Guidance
Enterprise ShareFile Storage Zones Controller zero-day may affect maritime logistics workflows; urgent patching and exposure review are advised. SecurityWeek
Federal alert broadened on Iran-linked OT targeting, relevant to port, shipboard, and offshore ICS/OT environments. The Record

topThreats.action: Potential data exposure and remote pathways into port IT/OT via cranes, scanners, and logistics platforms.
